Working at NLR

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description

The NLR Data Engineering Group is seeking a Graduate Intern to serve as a curator for the Marine & Hydrokinetic Data Repository (MHKDR) and support other related domain-specific data repositories. These data repositories provide public access to the outcomes of official Department of Energy (DOE) funded research in the geothermal and marine and hydrokinetic sectors as well as research and development activities in other technologies including water purification, the energy-water nexus, renewable energy systems, and alternative energy systems. Work will consist of curating individual data submissions and advising researchers and scientists on better organizing their project data for submission. Submissions frequently relate to computational fluid dynamics, mechanical engineering, wave and current monitoring, structural testing, and various types of MHK energy converters.

Curation includes the review of metadata provided with each data submission for accuracy, completeness, and relevance to the submitted files. Curation also includes the organization of disparate submissions, creating consistency amongst metadata fields, adoption and implementation of emerging data standards and requirements, and the addition of supplemental information that may assist the DOE in categorizing data submissions. When necessary, curators contact submitters directly to resolve any discrepancies or omissions detected during the review. Because many data submissions involve complex or open-ended organizational challenges, the intern should be comfortable working independently, evaluating datasets critically, and proposing practical data organization and metadata solutions. The intern may also have opportunities to support other energy research projects through data organization, analysis support, or documentation of datasets used in ongoing research activities.

The intern in this position is expected to contribute an average of 20 hours per week during semesters and 40 hours per week during breaks, including summer.

Key Responsibilities

Data curators review and enhance data submissions to ensure metadata quality, consistency, and usability. Responsibilities include:

- Curate marine and hydrokinetic datasets for metadata completeness, accuracy, and alignment with repository standards.

- Apply data standards and identify gaps or inconsistencies in submissions.

- Coordinate with data submitters to resolve issues and improve data quality and usability.

- Occasionally support energy research, including data management, analysis support, and literature review.

Our Team

The Data Engineering group is a multi-disciplinary team of data and software engineers, data scientists, and product developers that are at the forefront of developing advanced data solutions for strategic energy analysis at scale. Our work is focused on making energy data and software more accessible, usable, and actionable for researchers and engineers at NLR and beyond. You will join a team where everyone is striving to improve their knowledge of software development best-practices, while caring about creating the best possible solution to cutting edge problems.

Our team creates secure, reusable, and efficient code, while supporting a variety of teams:

- A collaborative, fast paced, and fun work environment.

- Endless opportunities to learn and grow from experienced professionals in both web development and renewable energy.

- Work developing cutting-edge projects and contributing to research in the renewable energy industry.

- A life-long desire to build better a future through technology and data.

Mission and Vision

NLR strives to achieve our vision of an affordable and secure energy future through our mission: leading research, innovation, and strategic partnerships to deliver integrated solutions for an affordable and secure energy future.

As the energy systems laboratory, we bridge foundational research with practical applications to ensure various energy sources, storage, buildings, transportation, and emerging technologies work together to lower energy costs, drive economic growth, bolster national security, and deliver abundant energy.

The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design.

As a part of the global research, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models, Big Data Visual Analytics, Explainable AI (XAI), Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision & Mixed Reality, Cloud Robotics, Data Science, AI System Engineering, Time-series Analysis. We develop scalable, intelligent, and trustworthy AIoT solutions for Bosch products and services in application areas such as automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, smart manufacturing, enterprise AI, health care, smart home and building solutions.

Job Description

We are looking for research interns interested in advancing foundation models for multimodal and sensor-rich environments. Our research explores how AI systems can learn generalizable representations from heterogeneous real-world data, including time series, audio, vision, and physical sensor signals, and transfer that knowledge across tasks and domains.

As an intern, you will work alongside Bosch researchers on open research problems at the intersection of multimodal learning, foundation models, and real-world sensing. You will have access to challenging datasets and applications from areas such as mobility, manufacturing, robotics, and intelligent systems, with opportunities to turn research ideas into publications and working prototypes.

What You’ll Work On

Your research may explore topics such as:

- Foundation models for time-series and Multimodal data
- Causal Analysis and evidence-based reasoning
- Learning shared representations across images, time series, and other sensing modalities
- Self-supervised learning from large-scale unlabeled sensor datasets
- Multimodal fusion and cross-modal representation learning
- Pre-training strategies for heterogeneous and asynchronous data
- Generative modeling and synthetic data for sensor-rich applications
- Adapting pretrained models to new sensors, tasks, and domains with limited labeled data
- Robust learning under missing modalities, noisy measurements, and distribution shifts
- Efficient multimodal models for real-world and edge deployment
- New architectures and evaluation methods for multimodal foundation models

You will formulate research questions, develop and evaluate new methods, build experimental prototypes, and work with Bosch researchers and domain experts to understand how these approaches behave on real-world problems. Strong research results may lead to publications at leading ML, AI, or signal-processing venues.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

- Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Machine Learning, AI, or a related field
- Research experience with time-series foundation models, multimodal models, or self-supervised learning
- Hands-on experience with PyTorch or similar frameworks
- Research or project experience with multimodal learning, time-series modeling, representation learning, foundation models, or signal processing
- Comfortable designing experiments and analyzing model behavior rather than only applying existing models
- Strong Python programming skills
- Ability to communicate research ideas clearly and work collaboratively

Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience working with real-world sensor and telemetry signals from radar, LiDAR, IMU, or other multivariate time series
- Experience with Transformers, generative models, contrastive learning, or cross-modal learning
- Experience adapting large pretrained models through fine-tuning, parameter-efficient methods, or transfer learning
- Familiarity with robustness, domain adaptation, missing-modality learning, or uncertainty estimation
- Publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICASSP, AAAI, or related conferences
- Open-source implementations or research projects demonstrating strong experimental skills

Additional Information

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans

*Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date.

BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics)

- FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology)
- AWIM (A World In Motion)

Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, type of degree, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, type of position, job location, etc. Your Hiring Manager can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process.

- Help determine each investor's preferred communication method and support next-best-action recommendations for the team.

- Keep investor data accurate by reconciling CRM records against internal investment schedules and flagging anomalies.

SQL, Hex, Python, Microsoft Excel, our investor CRM, Microsoft Teams and SharePoint, and AI assistants for analysis and documentation.

Qualifications

- Junior, senior, or master's student in Finance, Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Information Systems, or a related field.

- Working knowledge of SQL (SELECT, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY) and strong Excel skills.

- Some exposure to Python or R for data analysis.

- Excellent attention to detail, especially with financial data.

- Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.

- Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain numbers to non-technical audiences.

- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Nice to Have

- Experience with a BI tool (Hex, Power BI, Tableau, or similar).

- Interest in private credit, alternative investments, or wealth management.

- Basic statistics or forecasting, such as regression, time series, or A/B testing.

- Experience with a CRM (Salesforce, Dynamics, HubSpot, or similar).

What You'll Gain

- Hands-on experience with investor analytics and capital raising at a private credit firm.

- Practical skills in SQL, Python, BI, and analytical modeling.

- Mentorship from HFA leadership.

- A portfolio-ready project presented to company leadership at the end of the summer.

Perks & Benefits

Job Description

Winter Internship - January 18, 2027 - May 21, 2027 (must not have graduated before June 2027)

As a Product Engineering Intern you will support our Product Engineering team while gaining

hands‑on experience in the semiconductor industry. This role is designed for active students who

are pursuing an engineering degree and are interested in learning how products move from design

into manufacturing and production. You will work alongside experienced engineers, contribute to

engineering tasks, and gain exposure to product qualification, data analysis, and cross‑functional

collaboration. This is a learning‑focused role with structured mentorship and clear technical

development opportunities.

Role

- Work cross-functionally on development of BMICs and battery charger IC products.
- Assist Product Engineers with data collection and analysis of product test results.
- Support product temperature characterization, Guage R&R, and qualification activities.
- Learn evaluation and disposition techniques for ESD, Latchup, and HTOL qualifications.
- Prepare engineering documentation, reports and EBRs.
- Participate in team meetings and reviews to understand product development flow.
- Work on well‑defined digital and hands-on technical tasks or improvement projects.

Qualifications

- Active BS candidate with 2-3 years of coursework in Electronics or Electrical Engineering,
- preferred focus on IC design or fabrication. Rising junior or seniors only. (Must not have
- graduated before September 2027)
- Strong understanding of electronics and engineering fundamentals.
- Strong technical and computer skills.
- Strong understanding of basic lab instruments (power supplies, oscilloscopes, DMMs).
- Proficiency in MS office and Excel; Minitab or JMP preferred.
- Basic use of MATLAB, Python, C/C#, VBA, or similar language.
- Willingness to learn new software and skills, take feedback, and work as part of a fast-paced
- team.
- Self-motivated with strong engineering problem-solving skills.
- Ability to create plans for open-ended tasks.
- Attention to detail and organization.
- Ability to troubleshoot and ask questions when obstacles are met.
- Experience with Converters, DCDC, Buck Boost, etc a plus
